stemMd: Why does ordinary sound not propagate through a vacuum?

options.label: A
options.textMd: Sound requires electric charge on every molecule.

options.label: B
options.textMd: Sound consists only of visible light.

options.label: C
options.textMd: It requires a material medium to transmit mechanical disturbances.

options.label: D
options.textMd: Vacuum absorbs every possible electromagnetic wave.

explanationMd: Sound transmits oscillations through interactions among particles of a medium. A vacuum lacks those particles; this contrasts with electromagnetic waves, which need no material medium.

distractorRationale.e: A vacuum is not defined by absolute-zero temperature.
distractorRationale.d: Electromagnetic waves can propagate in vacuum.
